lines.english: He turned his thoughts to something else,
Wealthy Jakyp entrusted to Oshpur
The boy named Chong Jindi—Great Madcap.
Chyiyrdy wept and wailed,
Draping her belt around her neck,
Pleading, calling out, ‘Oshpur bai!’:
‘My dear Oshpur bai,
You were a giant dwelling in the valley,
You had charge of wealthy Jakyp’s many sheep.
We have great wealth, but no child;
This child we had when we were all but dead—
lines.note: The phrase literally says ‘seen when dead’; it appears to express how late or desperately awaited the child was.

lines.english: There is no way to curb his mischief.
I have made a silk coat; have him wear it.
Among the horses is Toruchaar;
Catch that noble steed and have him ride it.
Be sure to fasten a Kalmyk stone to the crown of his head.
lines.note: The nature of the ‘Kalmyk stone’ is unclear; the unusual image is retained literally.

lines.english: I have placed him in your hands as a sacred trust;
Care for him for another four years!’
Once Oshpur had taken the boy,
Once wealthy Jakyp had stayed behind there,
He set him on Toruchaar,
Clothed him in the ashes of silk,
lines.note: ‘Ashes of silk’ renders the wording literally; this may be an idiomatic description of a silk garment, but its precise sense is uncertain.

lines.english: And, trusting to fate, toward the sheep
Brave Oshpur led him away.
When Manas went to Oshpur,
He had not yet become Manas,
Your champion had not yet gained the name Manas.
